ORAL JUDGMENT :-
1) This is an Appeal under Section 173 of the Motor Kavita.
2/8 10 fa 589-15 Vehicles Act, 1988 (for short MV Act), by the Original Claimants against the Judgment and Award dated 27/10/2014 passed by the learned Motor Accident Claims Tribunal,
Wardha (for short 'Tribunal'), in the M.A.C.P. No.72 of 2013 by holding the deceased, who was the son of the Appellants, 50% liable for the Motor Vehicular Accident.
To say it in other words, the Appellants have challenged the impugned judgment to the extent of 50 contributory negligence.
Ajabrao S/O Ramaji Kubde And Another vs The Manager, Bharti Axa General ...

on 5 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/33748750/
1 2) Heard the learned Advocate for the Appellants and the learned Advocate for the Respondent No.1-Insurance Company.
None for the other respondents.
3) Perused the paper book.
The Appellants are the parents of deceased.
On 27th March, 2013, when deceased Sheshrao was travelling on his two wheeler and reached the Jam- Nagpur highway, the accident took place with the Motor Car, which was travelling from Jam to Nagpur.
The stop of the accident was the 'T' point.
The deceased succumbed to the injuries.
The Appellants filed the Claim Petition under Section 166 of the M.V.Act.
The Insurance Company and the Kavita.
3/8 10 fa 589-15 Respondent Nos.2 and 3 in the Claim Petition filed their respective Written Statements disputing the claim.
They pleaded that the accident was result of the contributory negligence.
The Appellant No.1 examined himself as the witness.
The Appellants brought on record the police papers in support of their claim.
The driver of the motor car, who was arrayed as respondent No.3 to the claim Petition filed his evidence/affidavit.

4) Appreciating the material available on record, the learned Tribunal decided the Claim Petition No.72 of 2013 quantifying the compensation of Rs.16,10,540/- with interest @ 75% per annum and held the deceased 50% responsible for the accident.
5) It is submitted by the learned Advocate for the Appellants that, no eye witness was examined by the respondents.
The Spot Panchnama, which was the part and parcel of the Police papers does not show the exact location of the spot of incident.
The deceased was not travelling on the highway.
The car driver should have been careful.
The offence was registered against the Car driver.
Learned Kavita.
Tribunal has not appreciated the material available on record and recorded the erroneous findings that, the deceased contributed to the accident to the extent of 50%.

The learned Advocate for theAppellant has relied on the decision of the Hon'ble Apex Court in Civil Appeal No.3465-3466 of 2025 (Prabhavati and ors. Vs. The Managing Director dated 28/02/2025 and decision of this Court in Branch Manager United India Insurance Company Vs. Vijay Vishnupant Karandikar and ors. reported in 2013(5) Mh.L.J. 775 in support of his contention.

6) It is submitted by the learned Advocate for the respondent No.1 Insurance Company that, the learned Tribunal has properly appreciated the material available on record and correctly arrived at the decision of contributory negligence by the deceased and hence no interference was called for.
7) In the case of Prabhavati and ors.Vs. The Managing Director (Supra), the contributory negligence of 25% considered by the High Court was held to be erroneous.
It was observed that, in the absence of any direct or Kavita.
5/8 10 fa 589-15 corroborative evidence on record, it cannot be assumed that the accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of both the vehicles.
In the Case of Branch Manager Vs. Vijay Vishnupant Karandikar and ors (supra) the police papers led to the inference that, the driver of the Motor Car drove the vehicle rashly and negligently.

sentences.text: 8) In the case at hand, admittedly, the Appellants were not the eye witnesses to the accident.
The Appellants based their claim on the police papers comprising First Information Report, Spot Panchnama etc.
The sketch of the accident is shown in the Spot Panchnama.
There is no dispute that, the car was on the highway.
It is also not in dispute that, the deceased was travelling on the small road touching the highway.
The deceased wanted to go towards or on the highway.
It is clear from the sketch of the spot of the accident as shown in the Spot Panchnama that, the small road from which the deceased was travelling on the motor cycle was touching the highway.

It is needless to state that, when one Kavita.
6/8 10 fa 589-15 drives or goes from one road to the another and more particularly on the highway,
necessary precautions are required to be taken.
9) Undisputedly, the crime for the Motor Vehicular Accident was registered against the driver of the said car, who was the respondent No.3 in the claim petition.

The respondent No.3 driver had filed his evidence/ affidavit before the Tribunal stating that, while he was driving the car, suddenly, the deceased came on the motor cycle on the road in the high speed and dashed to the car.
He stated that he was not at fault.
Undisputedly, the respondent No.3, who examined himself as a witness was not cross examined.
Therefore, it is clear that his evidence went unchallenged.
10) Perusal of the judgment passed by the learned Tribunal go to show that, it considered the marital available on record.

The relevant observations from the impugned judgement are reproduced below:-
"I find much substance in the arguments advanced on behalf of insurance company.
As afore-said, applicants have not examined eye- witness.
The evidence adduced by them is not sufficient to prove the manner in which Kavita.
7/8 10 fa 589-15 accident took place as pleaded by them.
The evidence adduced by them is not ruling out possibility of negligence on the part of deceased.

No doubt,
mere non-observance of traffic rules can not be held as contributory factor; but, in this case, observance of the traffic rule i. e. the driver coming from small road joining highway should give way to vehicle passing from the highway, should have been observed.
If that would have been observed then deceased could have avoided the accident.
The possibility of he coming on highway and Jeep also coming near him at the same time has not been ruled out by the applicants.
Applicants were duty bound to prove the sole negligence of opponent No.3.
Further as afore-said, testimony of OW Kiran is not fully believable, as he has not given some of the details of accident.
Therefore, this is a case of contributory negligence.
The case of negligence on the part of deceased has been pleaded by all the opponents.
At one place, they have said it was his sole negligence and opponent No.2 and 3 have also stated that he has contributed to the accident.

Hence, the ratio laid down in 2010 (1) ALL MR 754 is not applicable here on the contrary the ratio laid down in AIR 2003 SC 4182 is applicable here,
Ajabrao S/O Ramaji Kubde And Another vs The Manager, Bharti Axa General ... on 5 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/33748750/
3 wherein what amounts to negligence and contributory negligence has been explained in the same.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: When the exact material has not been placed by both the parties for apportionment of the negligence, then the circumstances are required to be considered.
Deceased was coming on the high way and therefore, he had responsibility to took for the traffic on the highway.
He appears to have failed in that duty.
Opponent No.3 was equally duty bound to control his vehicle Kavita.
8/8 10 fa 589-15 though he was proceeding from highway.

Hence, in my opinion,
both i. e. opponent No.3 and deceased Sheshrao were equally responsible (50:50) for the accident".
11) The said observations are based on the material available on record.
Considering the material available on record, the inference drawn and the conclusion reached by the learned Tribunal cannot be said to be perverse.
The said reasons are acceptable.
On re-appreciation of the material available on record, I find myself in agreement with the inference drawn by the learned Tribunal.
Hence, no interference is called for in the impugned judgment and Award .
Hence, the following order.
ORDER 1. The Appeal is dismissed.
2. R and P be sent back to the learned Tribunal.
( NEERAJ P. DHOTE, J.) Signed by: Kavita P Tayade
